purpose: Full candidate discovery log for the 2026-08 market-wide RAG storage screen. Every candidate considered is recorded here, including clean fails, so a future agent never silently rediscovers and re-tests the same dead end. 26 total: 23 researched this session, 3 (Turso, Zilliz, Pinecone) carried in from prior sessions and merged into this same comparison.
coverage_method: Named-vendor research (5 parallel Tier-1 agents covering specialist vector DBs, general databases with vector capability, and search platforms) plus an open-discovery pass (~30+ search queries across two independent search backends: Google-backed WebSearch and Exa semantic search) for new/overlooked 2025-2026 entrants. Every load-bearing claim was checked against the vendor's own official pages, not aggregators - this caught aggregators being flatly wrong about Meilisearch, Vectara, and Vectroid's actual free-tier terms.
coverage_limits: Not claimed as exhaustive - a brand-new, unindexed, no-SEO launch could be missed. ~13 further names were identified during discovery but not individually hard-gate-screened, named here for transparency about where the search stopped, not as a claim about their merit: Neo4j AuraDB, ArangoDB Oasis, YugabyteDB, KDB.AI, Oracle 23ai, MotherDuck, Google Firestore vector search, Amazon MemoryDB, ParadeDB, Marqo Cloud, Deep Lake/Activeloop, and generic Postgres/DBaaS clouds with pgvector support (Aiven, Elestio, Exoscale).

candidates.name: Pinecone Starter
candidates.session: prior (merged into this comparison per explicit user instruction - must not be excluded merely for being researched separately)
candidates.why_relevant: next candidate per the pre-existing fallback sequence after Turso and Zilliz both failed
candidates.outcome: SCREENING_PASS / BENCHMARK_PENDING / PRODUCTION_NOT_APPROVED - see shortlist.json

candidates.name: Neon (Postgres + pgvector)
candidates.why_relevant: mature pgvector foundation, potential automatic scale-to-zero
candidates.outcome: SCREENING_PASS_WITH_CAPACITY_RISK / BENCHMARK_PENDING - see shortlist.json

candidates.name: Weaviate Cloud
candidates.why_relevant: native BM25+hybrid search, purpose-built vector engine
candidates.outcome: UNKNOWN/CONDITIONAL - idle-suspension policy genuinely unresolved after two research passes; not promoted

candidates.name: LambdaDB
candidates.discovered_via: Exa semantic search: 'new serverless vector database startup launched 2025 2026 with permanent free tier'
candidates.why_relevant: disaggregated storage/compute architecture, no cluster to suspend by design, doc examples use 768-dim vectors specifically
candidates.outcome: UNKNOWN/CONDITIONAL - own live Quickstart page confirms 'LambdaDB Cloud is in public preview' as a whole product; gates 5-10 unresearched; not promoted

candidates.name: Lantern Cloud
candidates.discovered_via: WebSearch: 'reddit vector database recommendation... alternative Pinecone'
candidates.why_relevant: YC-backed pgvector cloud, most explicit anti-inactivity-suspension marketing claim found in the whole study ('a free tier that never pauses')
candidates.outcome: UNKNOWN/CONDITIONAL - free-tier storage cap genuinely unpublished after two real attempts (official docs, ToS, GitHub, Wayback Machine, YC page); not promoted

candidates.name: TiDB Cloud (Starter)
candidates.why_relevant: generous free quota, real ACID transactions
candidates.outcome: CONDITIONAL - every named hard gate resolves, but PingCAP's own docs call vector search 'experimental... not recommended for production'; documented fallback, not promoted

candidates.name: Cloudflare Vectorize
candidates.why_relevant: Cloudflare's Workers-native serverless model suggested possible transparent scale-to-zero
candidates.outcome: Soft-fail - 317% of the true-$0 free stored-dimension quota (5M free vs 15.86M needed at current scale); resolves for a flat ~$5/mo Workers Paid plan even at 3x growth; not $0 as specified

candidates.name: LanceDB Cloud
candidates.why_relevant: most technically capable candidate found on paper (genuine OCC/MVCC concurrency, confirmed strong consistency, native BM25)
candidates.outcome: FAIL - only official framing ties 'free' to beta status with usage-based pricing at GA; no post-GA free-tier commitment found anywhere, including a dead ToS PDF link; revisit if/when GA pricing is published

candidates.name: Vectroid
candidates.discovered_via: Exa semantic search + confirmed via targeted WebSearch
candidates.why_relevant: markets '100GB free forever,' legitimate company (Hazelcast founder, $2.45M seed, real HN thread and VC writeup)
candidates.outcome: FAIL - own ToS (Section 2, 'Inactive Accounts') has an explicit 60-day-inactivity-to-deletion clause directly contradicting the 'free forever... no catch' blog marketing; same marketing-vs-ToS gap pattern as Upstash Vector

candidates.name: Upstash Vector
candidates.why_relevant: well-known serverless vector DB
candidates.outcome: FAIL - own ToS (trust/terms.pdf) mandates deletion of free-plan resources after 1 week of no requests, no warning period, no restoration mechanism documented

candidates.name: Qdrant Cloud
candidates.why_relevant: popular open-source-backed vector DB
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official docs confirm free clusters auto-suspend after 1 week and auto-delete after 4 weeks of inactivity

candidates.name: Chroma Cloud
candidates.why_relevant: popular embedded/cloud vector DB
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official pricing describes a one-time $5 credit for new users, not a standing permanent free tier (though the near-zero usage cost for this workload's scale means the credit could plausibly last years - an economics point, not a permanence guarantee)

candidates.name: Redis Cloud Free
candidates.why_relevant: ubiquitous, has a vector search module (RediSearch/vector sets)
candidates.outcome: FAIL, doubly - 30MB storage cap (smaller than the ~63MB raw payload alone) AND official Redis Knowledge Base confirms 14-day inactivity triggers automatic, permanent, unrecoverable deletion with no backup - worse failure mode than Zilliz

candidates.name: Typesense Cloud
candidates.why_relevant: native BM25 + vector hybrid search
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official Help Center confirms a one-time, non-replenishing 720-hour (~30-day) trial; architecturally cannot offer a permanent free tier since a dedicated node is provisioned per cluster even for free users

candidates.name: Supabase (Postgres + pgvector)
candidates.why_relevant: popular managed Postgres with pgvector, same underlying tech as Neon
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official docs confirm free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity, requiring an explicit manual dashboard 'Resume project' click - same disqualifying pattern as Zilliz

candidates.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search (M0)
candidates.why_relevant: ubiquitous managed document DB with vector search
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official docs confirm 30-day auto-pause requiring manual resume; MongoDB's own deployment-options docs also steer M0 to 'testing queries' only, stating production vector search needs a paid M10+ cluster

candidates.name: DataStax Astra DB
candidates.why_relevant: Cassandra-based, vector search support
candidates.outcome: FAIL, most severe idle-policy failure of the whole study - official docs confirm 48-hour idle triggers hibernation, 30 consecutive days hibernated triggers automatic permanent deletion; even the API resume path returns 503 and requires a manual retry/poll loop over minutes

candidates.name: Couchbase Capella
candidates.discovered_via: WebSearch: 'Couchbase Capella free tier vector search 2026 permanent'
candidates.why_relevant: established DB recently added vector search plus 'perpetual' free-tier marketing language
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official docs confirm the free-tier cluster is deleted after 30 days of inactivity

candidates.name: Algolia (vector/NeuralSearch)
candidates.why_relevant: well-known hosted search platform
candidates.outcome: FAIL - vector/NeuralSearch capability is gated to the Elevate (enterprise, sales-only) tier; no free or self-serve paid tier includes vector search at all

candidates.name: Elastic Cloud (managed Elasticsearch)
candidates.why_relevant: BM25-native by design, mature hybrid search, real optimistic concurrency (_seq_no/_primary_term)
candidates.outcome: FAIL - 14-day trial only; a credit card becomes mandatory within the trial window to keep any deployment alive at all. (Self-managed Elasticsearch has a genuinely free Basic license, but that is the out-of-scope self-hosted family.)

candidates.name: AWS OpenSearch Service
candidates.why_relevant: widely-used managed OpenSearch
candidates.outcome: FAIL - AWS's own Free Tier taxonomy places this under '12 Months Free,' not 'Always Free'; standard rates apply automatically after 12 months

candidates.name: AWS OpenSearch Serverless
candidates.why_relevant: serverless variant of the above
candidates.outcome: FAIL - no free tier at all; minimum billable footprint estimated at roughly $174-350/month from the first collection

candidates.name: Aiven for OpenSearch
candidates.why_relevant: genuinely permanent, no-card free tier (confirmed via official docs)
candidates.outcome: FAIL - official docs state the service 'powers off automatically' on inactivity, requiring deliberate manual Console/CLI action to resume, with documented resume latency of 'a few minutes to a few hours'; auto-deletes after 180 days powered off

candidates.name: Bonsai (managed OpenSearch/Elasticsearch)
candidates.why_relevant: older blog/community content repeatedly claims a 'free forever Sandbox cluster'
candidates.outcome: FAIL - current official pricing page shows no free tier at all (cheapest plan $15/mo); the 'free forever' claims are stale and contradicted by the vendor's own current pricing page, exactly the trap this screen was designed to catch

candidates.name: Turso Cloud / libSQL
candidates.why_relevant: already-implemented and benchmarked candidate
candidates.outcome: FAIL - DiskANN retrieval quality (Recall@10=0.963 at 10k scale, below the 0.98 gate) and build-reliability (index build did not complete at the full 20,652-row production scale in either compression mode within a 30-min timeout); see ../turso/verdict.json

candidates.name: Zilliz Cloud Free (Milvus)
candidates.discovered_via: original candidate, pre-existing mandate fallback sequence
candidates.why_relevant: already-implemented and benchmarked candidate
candidates.outcome: FAIL - Free-tier clusters auto-suspend after 7 (per one vendor quote) or 14 (per another same-source quote) days of inactivity requiring explicit resume, with no synthetic keep-warm traffic permitted as a workaround; functional contract suite otherwise passed 9/10; see ../zilliz/verdict.json
